After generating completion o from prompt q using full diffusion denoising (left), we compute token-level log probabilities with a single forward pass per masking pattern (mid) and use the log-probability of one-step unmasking as our estimation. During each policy gradient update, we apply a random masking pattern to the prompt, creating q ′ , while keeping the completion fully masked (right). The gradient of colors in the per-token log probabilities demonstrates that each distinct masking pattern yields a different estimate of the per-token log probabilities. This serves as a form of regularization for policy optimization, allowing more gradient updates per batch and thereby reducing the number of online generations needed for RL training.
